absent: Enclave initialization and provisioning and permission and type change and removal ioctl semantics beyond dispatch routing.
Hardware instruction effects and encodings for enclave lifecycle operations.
Exact numeric values and bit positions for flags and masks and ioctl commands.
Full structure layouts with field offsets and sizes.
Background reclaimer thread startup and sleep and wakeup discipline beyond watermark wake.
Backing file lifecycle and truncation and teardown.
Concurrency rules for enclave page descriptor updates outside shown critical sections.
Address space attach and detach and version increment protocol.
Young tracking callback mechanics and page table walk details.
Error handling for security info validation and offset length validation helpers.

findings.text: The file operation entry serializes ioctl use per enclave with an exclusive busy marker that rejects overlapping calls, then routes each recognized enclave management command to its dedicated handler and reports unsupported commands distinctly before releasing the marker.

The add pages entry only proceeds on a created but uninitialized enclave, validates user length and alignment and offset range plus security info, then adds pages in page strides while yielding on schedule need and aborting on pending signals, finally reporting how much progress was made back to the caller.

Several helpers are shared across enclave, ioctl and reclaim compilation units, including enclave growth and shrink, backing allocation and release, EPC page allocation and release, virtual address translation, version address page allocation and slot management, young tracking and enclave lookup, processor mask building, and PTE zapping.

Creation refuses an already created enclave and a control structure whose size is not a power of two, ensures version address space with possible list linkage, sizes anonymous backing to cover payload plus control plus metadata overhead, allocates the control page, issues the hardware create step with zeroed page info except payload references, records base and size and attributes with a restricted unprivileged mask and optional debug marking, and publishes the created marker only after success with ordered unwind on failure.

The virtual address of an EPC page is derived from its owning section base plus a stride multiple where the index comes from the descriptor offset within the section descriptor array divided by descriptor extent.

Backing retrieval fetches separate content and control pages where the control location is placed after the enclave extent plus control extent and advances by a fixed per page control record extent, with sub page offset retained for the control fragment.

Age scanning walks the enclave address space roster and deems a page idle only when every attached address space reports its mapping as not recently accessed, while lookup succeeds only for mappings tagged with the enclave operations and later ownership is confirmed against the requesting enclave.

Per node free list mutation and page state and ownership updates occur under the node spin protection with global free count adjustment outside the critical section, distinguishing poisoned pages onto a separate list and clearing free state on removal.

Active reclaim list edits occur under dedicated reclaimer spin protection with reference held on the owning enclave, hardware block and writeback occur under the enclave mutex, roster traversal occurs under sleepable read side protection with address space lifetime pinning and read locking of the address space lock, and processor mask building follows the same roster discipline.

EPC allocation loops attempting immediate node aware retrieval then, when unsuccessful, fails if no reclaimable pages remain or reclaim is disallowed or a signal is pending, otherwise invokes synchronous reclaim and reschedules before retrying, and finally wakes the background reclaimer when the free count drops beneath a low watermark while reclaimable pages remain.

Reclaim proceeds in collection then preparation then blocking then writeback phases: it detaches a bounded batch while dropping untracked pages whose owners are vanishing, keeps only aged pages with allocated backing marked as under reclaim and requeues the rest, unmaps translations and issues the hardware block step, then writes each survivor to backing, clears its link, decrements the child tally, releases backing references and untracks and frees the slot, with special handling to evict the control page once the last child has gone on an initialized enclave.

Version address accounting increments a page tally and materializes a fresh tracking page only on slot boundary, links it to the enclave roster and undoes the tally and linkage on failure, while eviction consumes the head tracking slot and retires full tracking pages to the roster tail, and writeback retries tracking establishment then hardware fencing with cross processor notification before either recording the slot in the page descriptor or releasing the slot on persistent failure.

Observed groupings include an enclave anchor carrying flags and page tally and version roster and backing reference and control link and base plus size plus attributes, an EPC page carrying section index and owner link and poison and tracking flags, a version page carrying EPC link and occupancy bitmap, a backing handle carrying content and control page links plus sub page offset, and a hardware page info bundle carrying guest address plus payload plus metadata plus control references.

Hazards include overlapping ioctl use, creation replay, unaligned or out of range add requests, allocation exhaustion, signal interruption with partial progress, lost address space races handled by versioned PTE zapping retry, poisoned EPC pages segregated from reuse, untracked writeback needing fencing and inter processor kick, and hardware failures surfaced through warnings rather than silent success.

The ioctl interface exposes distinct management commands for creation, page addition, initialization, provisioning, permission restriction, type modification and page removal, alongside enclave state markers for ioctl busy, created, debug and initialized plus reclaim tracking and busy reclaim markers, page type markers for control and version address pages, and attribute markers including debug and unprivileged mask semantics.

Hardware invocation results distinguish faulted completions via a dedicated flag with trap number extraction, treat page fault traps as non failures while other faults and nonzero statuses count as failures, and expose a distinct not tracked status that triggers tracking establishment before retry.

Translation invalidation snapshots a roster version, traverses under read side protection with lifetime pinning and address space read locking while unmapping only matching enclave mappings, then repeats the whole pass when the version changed, paired with ordering barriers against concurrent roster insertion.

Node aware allocation prefers the current node when it hosts enclave memory and otherwise starts from the next hosting node and cycles through hosting nodes until a page is found or every hosting node has been tried.

Backing charge attribution uses the current task memory context in normal context and otherwise searches the enclave roster for a live address space to charge, falling back to ambient context when none remains, with active context switched only around the backing fetch.

Slot allocation selects the lowest clear occupancy bit and encodes it as a byte offset multiple, release clears the corresponding bit, fullness means no clear bit remains, and a build time assertion ties the slot total to the descriptor offset mask coverage.
